import view

def test_basic():
    v = view.View()
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    assert v.get_loading() == False
    # finish with same id
    rows1 = [1,2]
    assert v.finish(id1, rows1) == True
    assert v.rows == rows1
    # second begin
    id2 = v.begin('q2')
    # finish with old id should return False
    assert v.finish(id1, [3]) == False
    # finish with new id should succeed
    rows2 = [4,5]
    assert v.finish(id2, rows2) == True
    assert v.rows == rows2
    # copy rows after first finish
    copy1 = v.copy_accepted_rows()

    # after second finish rows2

    assert copy2 == rows2
    # notes preservation

    # begin clears loading errors but keeps existing rows until valid finish
    # error should be None after begin
    # finish with duplicate id (same as current) should return False? spec: older or duplicate replies return False. Duplicate means same id as current? Probably duplicate finish call with same id already used should return False after first valid finish. We'll test: after first valid finish, calling finish with same id again should return False.
    assert v.finish(id1, [6]) == False
    # notes still present
    assert v.notes['job1'] == 'note1'
    # loading flag
    assert v.loading == False

def test_stale_finish():
    v = view.View()
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    # do not finish yet, start another begin
    id2 = v.begin('q2')
    # finish id1 (stale) should return False
    rows1 = [1]
    assert v.finish(id1, rows1) == False
    # finish id2 should succeed
    rows2 = [2]
    assert v.finish(id2, rows2) == True
    assert v.rows == rows2
    # notes preserved
    v.notes['a'] = 'b'
    assert v.notes['a'] == 'b'

def test_clear_error():
    v = view.View()
    v.error = 'some error'
    v.loading = True
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    assert v.error is None
    assert v.loading == False
    rows1 = [1]
    assert v.finish(id1, rows1) == True
    # error cleared

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_basic()
    test_stale_finish()
    test_clear_error()
    print('All tests passed')
